newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Seventh Russia beet test shows 15.5% sugar content.
newsitem.headline: Seventh Russia beet test shows 15.5% sugar content.

text.p: Russia's seventh sugar beet test showed an average sugar content of 15.5 percent, the same level as at this time in 1995, the head of the Rossakhsvyokla sugar beet producers' association said on Monday.
Mikhail Sushkov provided the following data for the September 20 test, which the association added to its original testing schedule:
Sushkov said his forecasts for the beet harvest had not changed, despite harvest delays from rainy weather. "Our forecast for the beet harvest is 17.1 million tonnes," he said.
Russia had gathered beets from 119,000 hectares as of September 23, down from 387,000 at the same time a year earlier, which Sushkov attributed to rain and a lack of harvesting equipment.
Russia had sown 1.015 million hectares to beets in 1996, he said.
But he said there was no reason to fear sugar content of unharvested beets would be affected by the delay.
He said his predicted yield for the 1996 crop remained unchanged -- 16.0 tonnes per hectare, down from 17.5 tonnes in 1995.
Yields on crops gathered as of September 23 averaged 17.4 tonnes per hectare, versus 18.0 tonnes at the same time a year earlier.
Last year's sugar beet output was officially 19.1 million tonnes.
Sushkov said this was the final test of weight and sugar content of the 1996 beet crop.
